claims.text: A data-driven machine-learning model can rapidly identify promising refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
The proposed model is trained on high-fidelity experimental and simulation data.
Machine learning can identify RHEAs with intrinsically enhanced strength.
Machine learning can identify RHEAs with intrinsically enhanced ductility.
Machine learning can identify RHEAs with lower density.
The proposed ML approach is faster than traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation-based screening.
The relevant RHEAs consist of multiple principal elements in a predominantly BCC matrix.
A curated dataset annotated with strength, ductility, and density can be used to train a neural-network or ensemble model for RHEA design.
Ambient- and high-temperature measurements are representative of conditions relevant to refractory applications.
The ML model captures composition–microstructure interactions such as local lattice distortion and phase stability.
Local lattice distortion and phase stability mediate RHEA strength and ductility.
The model maps nonlinear relationships between elemental ratios and strength, ductility, and density.
An ML-assisted method can replace costly thermodynamic-integration calculations with more efficient calculations.
The ML model can rapidly screen a vast RHEA compositional space for optimal formulations.
ML-designed RHEAs will show statistically significant strength improvements over alloys designed using conventional thermo-kinetic methods.
ML-designed RHEAs will show statistically significant ductility improvements over alloys designed using conventional thermo-kinetic methods.
ML-designed RHEAs will have reduced density relative to alloys designed using conventional thermo-kinetic methods.
The method's effectiveness depends on the quality and scope of its training data.
Predictions outside the training compositional domain may be less reliable.
Incomplete or biased datasets and overfitting may limit generalizability until experimental validation is performed.
